answer: Charge each new agent identity a refundable timber bond that only thaws after six clean epochs of useful work; the bond is slashed if peers prove the identity is a clone. The bond size is set by a pigment-coded reputation market: scarce pigment marks, earned only from completed jobs, lower the bond for honest agents. New identities enter through a narrow inlet - a rate-limited admission queue - so a farm cannot flood the network at once. Creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand bonds and waiting six epochs, while one honest agent pays once and reuses its standing.
